title: Muse Ember Pricing: Cost per 1M Tokens (2026)
summary: Muse Ember pricing includes current rates and per-token costs. Use this to evaluate whether the model fits your budget and how it compares to alternatives.
body_markdown:
## Muse Ember Compared with Its Closest Alternatives


At 100M tokens a month Muse Ember **only ties two rivals on price** and costs more than three others, yet it is the cheapest small model per finished benchmark task.


In the table below, from[LLM API Comparison](https://llmapicomparison.com/cheapest/) , the monthly bill at 100M tokens puts Muse Ember, Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna on the same $18, so the monthly bill alone can't separate them.


Model Monthly bill at 100M tokens


Muse Ember $18


Claude Haiku 5.5 $18


GPT-6 Luna $18


M3 Mercury $15


Mistral Small 3.2 $14


Ministral 3 3B $10


I read the 100M tokens as the 4:1 input-to-output mix used earlier, though the source doesn't state its own. On that reading $18 per 100M works out to about $0.18 per 1M blended, which is the figure to hold against your own cost-per-million calculation.


Cost per task is where the three-way tie breaks.


### When Muse Ember wins on cost


On xhigh,[Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/meta-s-muse-ember-is-the-cheapest-model-scoring-36-on-the-intelligence-index) puts Muse Ember at $0.12 per benchmark task, and at $0.14 on max.


Xhigh and max are reasoning-effort settings, meaning how much the model thinks before it answers. More effort uses more output tokens, so cost per task rises with the setting.


A benchmark task is one complete problem from the test suite, run through to a graded answer.


The 3.4x and 5x ratios below divide by Ember's xhigh figure, and I'm treating the Haiku and DeepSeek numbers as xhigh runs too, since the source doesn't label them otherwise.


Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.41 per task, about 3.4 times Ember's xhigh figure, so **the identical $18 bill hides a large gap** in what each task costs you.


DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, at $0.60 per task, costs five times as much, which means you can run only one-fifth as many tasks on the same budget.


If you pay per completed job rather than per token, Ember is the clear pick.


### When an alternative is cheaper


On raw token volume, three models undercut Ember. M3 Mercury saves $3 a month, Mistral Small 3.2 saves $4 and Ministral 3 3B **saves $8, which is 44% off Ember's $18** .


> If you pay per completed job rather than per token, Ember is the clear pick.


At 100M tokens those are small dollars, and none of the three has a per-task figure here, so a lower token bill doesn't prove a lower cost per task.


One cent is the margin with GPT-6 Luna, the closer call: its max setting costs $0.15 per task against Ember's $0.14. Across 100,000 tasks that's $1,000, which matters at scale but isn't decisive for a small team.
